data.title: Start here
data.body:
# Start here: sharingu

sharingu is a closed loop for everything happening in an organisation. Contributions come from many kinds of people and
from their AI tools; the MCP turns each one into structured records; the app shows them; people decide on them; what is
still missing feeds the next contribution.

## The model (owner, 2026-09-30)

- **The MCP is the only input.** Your AI client reads the input where it lives and files it through sharingu's MCP door.
- **sharingu holds its own truth, in D1:** goals, the aim, questions and their rulings, checks and grades, cards, the
  model (screens, doors, tables, flows, gaps), the GTM template, docs.
- **Everything is live.** A write shows on the app at once; there is no publish step. Versions are snapshots on demand.
- **One product; projects differ only by data.**

## The three loops (the beta proof)

1. `holes` -> file what is missing -> it shows, and the item closes.
2. `decisions` -> `respond` with an option -> the question shows decided (owner) or answered (member).
3. checks -> `submit_grade` with proof -> the check shows graded on its goal and lights its node on the Map.

## Where to look in this project

- **Goals:** the road to beta (Stages A-C, sprints 1-3) and the marketplace launch after it.
- **Decisions:** the owner's rulings since the re-architecture (2026-09-30), and the questions still open.
- **Build:** the work of sprints 1-3, one contribution per commit, each with when it really happened.
- **Map:** the product's model and its architecture.

## How we work

One sprint, one branch; vertical slices (table -> MCP write -> the screen), each committed when the smoke is green; one
review at sprint end; forks go to the owner as MCQs. In the repo the plan is `docs/plan/`: `BETA.md`, then
`README.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `SPRINTS.md`.

data.title: Positioning
data.body:
# Positioning

Source: the owner's sharingu team context pack (version 6, as of 1 Oct 2026).

**Positioning:** Your agents connect the tools. sharingu connects the work to company goals.

## The ecosystem USP [Founder-described direction, 29 Sep 2026]
Your agents connect the tools; sharingu connects the work to company goals. People continue in compatible desktop or CLI
agents. Those agents use their existing authorized connections to services. sharingu supplies a shared contribution
process and company context through its own connection, and guides how work is shaped and filed.

## Plain product description [Founder-selected direction, checked 28 Sep 2026]
sharingu is a shared company brain that connects people's and agents' contributions, decisions and evidence to company
goals. Teams should be able to keep their compatible tools while carrying useful context forward. The longer-term
ambition is a unified workspace for knowledge, projects, GTM and operations.

## The hook [Proposal]
AI helps everyone produce more work. sharingu helps the company carry that work forward.

## Working vocabulary [Suggested wording]
External hook: "Turn AI work into contributions your company can build on." Product explanation: "Shared contribution
workflows across tools and teams." Technical shorthand: "contribution shaping and evaluation."

## Boundaries
- Lead the differentiation with work-specific contribution shapes, goal/dependency wiring, evidence readiness and
  reusable handoffs. Memory, graphs, schemas, MCP and generic workflow automation alone are not unique.
- Do not imply arbitrary SaaS credentials or permissions transfer to sharingu, that all clients interoperate
  automatically, or that every contribution completes a goal.
- Marketplace distribution is planned language only; no ChatGPT or Claude marketplace availability is claimed.

data.body:
# The first customer

Source: the owner's sharingu team context pack (version 6, as of 1 Oct 2026).

## The first customer to pursue [Founder-selected direction, checked 28 Sep 2026]
Initial focus: small product teams, studios and technical consultancies where founders, developers and business leads
already use AI. The 5-100-person band remains a research hypothesis rather than a strict product limit. Start with one
repeated handoff; keep the company-wide vision. This is the chosen go-to-market focus, not a verified description of
every pilot.

## First-session success [Founder-selected direction, checked 28 Sep 2026]
Create one real goal, add a useful contribution and let another person or agent pick it up. The goal is a successful
handoff, not completing a setup checklist or importing every existing document.

## Activation definition to test [Proposal]
An organization is activated when two different people, or a person and an agent acting for another contributor,
complete a useful handoff against the same real goal. Measure the time from onboarding to that event. Mere sign-up,
connection or generated text does not count.

data.title: The business model
data.body:
# The business model

Source: the owner's sharingu team context pack (version 6, as of 1 Oct 2026).

## Chosen direction: open core + hosted service [Founder-selected direction, checked 28 Sep 2026]
Build a genuinely useful open-source core. The first paid offer should focus on managed hosting, dependable operation,
team administration and support. Later business capabilities can follow customer needs. Released code and licence scope
still need verification: a public repository, licence and open-source release date have not been confirmed.

## Why someone would pay [Founder-selected direction, checked 28 Sep 2026]
Convenient managed hosting, reliable operation, team administration and support. Backups, synchronization, advanced
governance and deployment options should be scoped and tested before they are offered. This is the commercial direction,
not a statement that every paid capability is available now.

## Free should have a clear purpose [Proposal]
Use a free contributor beta to learn from real goals and handoffs. A community edition can make experimentation and
integrations easier. Hosting and model usage still have costs; decide included limits or bring-your-own-model
arrangements before promising free usage at scale.

## When to test monetization [Proposal]
Begin willingness-to-pay conversations during the free beta and offer a paid hosted plan when several independent teams
repeat the workflow and request ongoing service.

## Costs to measure [Proposal]
Hosting/storage, model or agent execution paid by sharingu, integration maintenance, support and onboarding per
organization. A measured gross margin is not meaningful at zero revenue. CAC and LTV are unknown.

## Status [Founder-reported, 28 Sep 2026]
No payments have been received. Ryuk Labs owns sharingu and its IP.

data.title: The pricing experiment
data.body:
# The pricing experiment

Source: the owner's sharingu team context pack (version 6, as of 1 Oct 2026).

## Pricing experiment [Proposal]
After repeat usage is visible, test hosted workspace offers around $99, $199 and $299 per organization/month. These are
research prompts, not published plans. Explore small-team bundles rather than charging for every agent identity. The
market model uses $199 as an illustrative average, not validated willingness to pay.

## Boundaries
- No price is launched; no revenue-sharing percentage or enterprise price has been set.
- The founder-selected paid value is managed hosting, reliable operation, team administration and support
  (see gtm/business-model.md).

data.title: Distribution and channels
data.body:
# Distribution and channels

Source: the owner's sharingu team context pack (version 6, as of 1 Oct 2026).

## Global ambition, relationships first [Founder-selected direction, checked 28 Sep 2026]
Build a global product. Start hands-on adoption through the founder's existing network in the UAE and beyond, alongside
contributor communities. This does not establish where the existing three teams are based.

## Open-source distribution loop [Founder-selected direction, checked 28 Sep 2026]
Lead with small contributor cohorts, useful public demonstrations and introductions through founders, studios and
technical operators. Contributors test real workflows, report failures, improve documentation and contribute
integrations. Open-source publication needs a defined licence and release scope. Measure recurring organizational use
and useful handoffs, not just stars or sign-ups.

## Partner-led distribution [Proposal]
Agencies, product studios, fractional CTOs and AI implementation teams can introduce sharingu into delivery work they
already manage. Offer a bounded joint beta and onboarding help first. Referral or revenue-share terms are negotiable
proposals, not current commitments.

## Call-first funnel [Proposal]
Researched profile -> relevant approach -> positive reply -> booked call -> held call -> demo or pilot -> repeat use ->
paid evaluation. Track counts and reasons; no response-rate guarantee. Email opens are not a reliable success measure.

kinds.proofConcrete: the positive reply or the booked call (the call-first funnel)
the published post's link; nothing is posted without the founder's instruction
the submitted form's confirmation; nothing is submitted without the founder's instruction
the partner's reply to a bounded joint beta
the held call where the demo was shown

proofRule.rule: A link or record of what actually went out and what came back. Do not send outreach, submit applications, publish social posts or change funding terms without the founder's instruction. Email opens are not a success measure.

outcomeModel.expected: the funnel stage it aims for (researched profile -> approach -> positive reply -> booked call -> held call -> demo or pilot -> repeat use -> paid evaluation)
outcomeModel.actual: the stage reached, with the reason; counts, never a response-rate guarantee
